target_customer: Operators of stadiums, prisons, airports and private sites that want to stop unauthorized drones
problem: Commercial drones could enter sensitive airspace and existing countermeasures were military focused, detection only, or jamming that disturbs other communications.
business_model: Hardware counter drone box sold for about 30 thousand dollars per Bloomberg plus software add ons
product_category: Counter drone detection and takeover hardware

founders.name: Nimo Shkedy
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO and co-founder in TechCrunch (2016-08-17) and the YC launch post (2016-09-06); the company was first incorporated as Airfence.

founders.name: Gilad Beeri
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO; TechCrunch calls him CTO. The YC page says the product was developed by experts from the Israel Defense Forces, a company claim.

competitors.name: SRC Inc.
competitors.what: Defense counter drone systems that could move to the consumer market

technical_complexity.rationale: Detecting drones by radio signals and issuing return to controller commands across brands needed RF engineering and reverse engineering of drone protocols.

defensibility.rationale: Founders planned a threat library R and D advantage, comparing it to antivirus software, but rivals including DroneShield already sold detection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Counter drone became a crowded defense market; no acquisition of ApolloShield found.

market_need_then: Bloomberg (2016-09-01) described rising concern over rogue drones and an emerging market of nets, ray guns and trained birds.

branding.domain_note: Uses apolloshield.com exact match; company was first called Airfence, no detail on the switch.

identity.voice_and_tone: Security focused with a defense heritage claim

rebrands.why: Not sourced; TechCrunch and a profile note the earlier name

branding.community_and_virality: Bloomberg and TechCrunch covered the launch; no merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch press in 2016 but no sourced evidence of lasting brand strength.

outcome_analysis: ApolloShield launched at YC in 2016 with a plug and play box that sends drones back to their operator and is still listed as active and claims customers in over 25 countries. Funding is only partly visible and no exit was found. Competition from detection and net based rivals grew, and the claims about customers come from the company itself.
notes: TechCrunch says about 500 thousand dollars raised to date, recorded as other since no stage is stated and it may include YC money. Calcalist style profiles list a 2.5 million dollar seed in October 2016 and a total of 2.62 million with Root Ventures and Igor Ryabenkiy; CB Insights lists only 120 thousand dollars; none of these were verified, so they are not recorded. Company site fetch was rate limited.
